\lcCategory{With the paper's hypotheses; Lean proves a narrower conclusion.}{15}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}{2.3.1} & Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails\newline{\footnotesize Proved with the lemma's hypotheses except part of the closing smoothing remark: spatial smoothing of the covariance appears only as membership of the Gaussian factor in the multiplier class (its spectral identification is not formalized), and Green smoothing is identified with the smoothed norm only in dimension one. The $N_0$ mass identity under Green smoothing holds in every dimension.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}{4.1.2} & Auxiliary mask norm\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves, under \lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1} and $\Gamma\neq0$, that $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, the ball bound \lcRef{Equation}{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}{4.1.5} uniformly in $R>0$, and \lcRef{Equation}{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}{4.1.6} for a separable complex Hilbert space $H$ (indeed any complex Banach space) with integrability and a finite right side; the clause for a real $H$ after complexification is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:variational-global-mean}{7.3.2} & Global regularity of the original mean\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the display \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-global-mean}{7.3.3} on $I=[0,1]$ ($0\le h_s\le M$ and $\|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|$, with integrability, continuity in $x$ and a joint Lipschitz bound); the first sentence, that every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded, is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3} & The unmasked Rayleigh rate\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves, with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, the statements about the Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}: for $\lambda$ defined as its square root, a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and $I_\Psi$ positive and finite; the operator statements ($H_s$ self-adjoint, form domain $H^1$, spectral bottom $E_s$, $\lambda=\sqrt{-E_s}$) are not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:variational-control-dilation}{7.3.5} & Radon and Rayleigh dilation\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the bijection and the four identities with the section's hypotheses (\lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1}, $\Gamma\neq0$, $a=\alpha_0$) and nothing supplied, for the variance in its integral form and the rate defined as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}; their identification with $\E W(\Psi)^2$ (\lcRef{Lemma}{L:compact-raw-profile}{6.3.6}) and $\sqrt{-E_s}$ (\lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3}) is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-positive-scores}{7.3.6} & Intrinsic variational lower bounds\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the proposition with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, including the boundedness of the value sets and the supremum statements ($S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ finite, positive, equal to $c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$), with $\lambda$ the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum and $v_\Psi$ the cost in its integral form; $Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-static-controls}{8.2.2} & Smooth temporal controls\newline{\footnotesize $\lambda$ is the square root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient, and $I_\Psi$, $v_\Psi$ are given by their integral formulas (identification with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\E W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized); \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-static-score}{8.2.2} is proved both in the form that every number below the bound is exceeded by some admissible score and in its supremum form, with nothing supplied.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}{8.2.4} & The finite smooth spatial ratio\newline{\footnotesize \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-smooth-score}{8.2.4} is proved, with nothing supplied, both in the form that every $y$ below the bound is exceeded by some $I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2$ and as a bound on the supremum, with $\lambda$ the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum and $v_\Psi$ given by its integral formula (identification with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\E W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized). $R_0<\infty$ is proved by \lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-fourier-bound}{8.2.3}.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-four-linear}{8.2.5} & The physical four-linear extension\newline{\footnotesize Joint continuity of $C_4$ on $(H^1)^4$ is proved along convergent sequences ($H^1$ convergence of the four profiles, that is $L^2$ convergence of each function and of its weak gradient), not for a topology on $(H^1)^4$; continuity of $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and of the square pairings is not restated separately (they are $C_4(f,f,f,f)$ and $C_4(f,f,h,h)$).}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-energy-map}{8.2.6} & The spatial energy and static lower variational expression\newline{\footnotesize \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-static-energy-score}{8.2.10} is proved, with nothing supplied, both in an existential form (every $y$ below $M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}})$ is exceeded by some $I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2$) and in its supremum form, with $\lambda$ the square root of the Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4} and $v_\Psi$ by its integral formula (their identification with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\E W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized).}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:occupation-physical-class}{8.2.8} & The full physical occupation class\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves measurability, independence of the representatives, \lcRef{Equation}{E:occupation-physical-bound}{8.2.13} (with $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$) and \lcRef{Equation}{E:occupation-own-energy}{8.2.14} (with $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$) over the class $\mathcal{O}$ modelled by fields with jointly measurable representatives of $g$ and of its gradient; the construction of such representatives from strongly $H^1$-measurable fields (a simple-function approximation) and the converse are not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:tube-rayleigh-tail}{10.2.7} & Exact Rayleigh tail bound\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the bound with integrability and the finite head integral; the ``In particular'' application to the coarse-envelope bound of another proposition is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:positive-raw-embedding}{11.2.1} & Inclusion into the covariance space and the smooth mean\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the variance identity in integral form (for $\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ the integral of $|s-t|^{-a}B_\Gamma(\Psi_s,\Psi_t)$ over $I^2$ is genuine and equals $v_\Psi\ge0$) and the row bound $\int_I|s-t|^{-a}\ud t\le K_0$ with the scalar Schur bound; $H_t$, $H_I$, the map $J_G$ and the mean identity for the uniform $E$ mean are not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Theorem}{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling}{11.3.4} & The computed occupation ceiling\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves $\mathfrak{c}I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2\le U_{\mathfrak{c}}$ for every nonnegative smooth control and $S_{\mathfrak{c}}^{\mathrm{pos}}\le U_{\mathfrak{c}}$, for every $\mathfrak{c}>0$, with the constant $K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}$, an upper bound of $C_{\rm occ}$, in place of $C_{\rm occ}$ (a larger ceiling); $\lambda$ is the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum and $v_\Psi$ the integral-form cost. The class $\mathcal{O}$, $A(g)$, $C_{\rm occ}$, the second form through $\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}$ and $C_2(\Gamma,a)\le U_2$ are not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Corollary}{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}{11.3.5} & A common spatial-energy bracket\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves, with the section's hypotheses (\lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1}, $\Gamma\neq0$, $a=\alpha_0$) and nothing supplied, \lcRef{Equation}{E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}{11.3.9} and the comparison for the variational value $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$ in place of $C_2(\Gamma,a)$ (identified by \lcRef{Theorem}{T:intrinsic-second-moment}{11.2.6}), with the energy $D_{1/2}(K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{2/(2-\alpha)}$ in place of $\mathcal{E}_{1/2}^{\mathcal{O}}$ in the comparison; $\lambda$ is the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum.}
\end{lcTable}
